module

public import MathlibExt.Analysis.Matrix.HermitianPseudoInverse

/-!
# Uniqueness of the finite Hermitian spectral pseudoinverse

The four Penrose equations identify a computed matrix with the existing
Matrix.spectralPseudoInverse. This is used to compare a grounded graph inverse with the
spectral reciprocal; no alternative pseudoinverse definition is introduced.

Source: R. Penrose, *A generalized inverse for matrices*, Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 51
(1955), 406–413, the four-equation characterization.
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

namespace Matrix

variable {𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

/-- A matrix satisfying the four Penrose equations is the native spectral pseudoinverse. -/
theorem eq_spectralPseudoInverse_of_penrose {A X : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hA : A.IsHermitian)
    (hAXA : A * X * A = A) (hXAX : X * A * X = X)
    (hAX : (A * X).IsHermitian) (hXA : (X * A).IsHermitian) :
    X = spectralPseudoInverse A := by
  let P := spectralPseudoInverse A
  have hAPA : A * P * A = A := hA.mul_spectralPseudoInverse_mul
  have hPAP : P * A * P = P := hA.spectralPseudoInverse_mul_spectralPseudoInverse
  have hAP : (A * P).IsHermitian := hA.conjTranspose_mul_spectralPseudoInverse
  have hPA : (P * A).IsHermitian := hA.conjTranspose_spectralPseudoInverse_mul
  have hAXAP : (A * X) * (A * P) = A * P := by
    calc
      (A * X) * (A * P) = (A * X * A) * P := by simp only [Matrix.mul_assoc]
      _ = A * P := by rw [hAXA]
  have hAPAX : (A * P) * (A * X) = A * X := by
    calc
      (A * P) * (A * X) = (A * P * A) * X := by simp only [Matrix.mul_assoc]
      _ = A * X := by rw [hAPA]
  have hleft : A * X = A * P := by
    have h := congrArg Matrix.conjTranspose hAXAP
    simp only [conjTranspose_mul, hAP.eq, hAX.eq] at h
    exact hAPAX.symm.trans h
  have hXAPA : (X * A) * (P * A) = X * A := by
    calc
      (X * A) * (P * A) = X * (A * P * A) := by simp only [Matrix.mul_assoc]
      _ = X * A := by rw [hAPA]
  have hPAXA : (P * A) * (X * A) = P * A := by
    calc
      (P * A) * (X * A) = P * (A * X * A) := by simp only [Matrix.mul_assoc]
      _ = P * A := by rw [hAXA]
  have hright : X * A = P * A := by
    have h := congrArg Matrix.conjTranspose hPAXA
    simp only [conjTranspose_mul, hPA.eq, hXA.eq] at h
    exact hXAPA.symm.trans h
  calc
    X = X * A * X := hXAX.symm
    _ = P * A * X := by rw [hright]
    _ = P * A * P := by rw [Matrix.mul_assoc, hleft, ← Matrix.mul_assoc]
    _ = P := hPAP

end Matrix

module

public import MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Complex.UnitVector
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Matrix.PosDef
import Mathlib.Analysis.Matrix.Hermitian

@[expose] public section

open scoped ComplexOrder BigOperators
open Complex Matrix

namespace Matrix

variable {n : Type*} [Fintype n]

public theorem not_posSemidef_iff_exists_unitVector_neg {M : Matrix n n ℂ}
    (hM : M.IsHermitian) :
    ¬ M.PosSemidef ↔ ∃ ψ : Complex.UnitVector n, star ψ.coord ⬝ᵥ (M *ᵥ ψ.coord) < 0 := by
  constructor
  · intro hNot
    have h_not_forall : ¬ ∀ x : n → ℂ, 0 ≤ star x ⬝ᵥ (M *ᵥ x) := by
      intro hAll
      exact hNot (posSemidef_iff_dotProduct_mulVec.mpr ⟨hM, hAll⟩)
    classical
    have h_exists : ∃ x : n → ℂ, ¬ 0 ≤ star x ⬝ᵥ (M *ᵥ x) := by
      by_contra h
      have h_all : ∀ x : n → ℂ, 0 ≤ star x ⬝ᵥ (M *ᵥ x) := by
        intro x
        by_contra hx
        exact h ⟨x, hx⟩
      exact h_not_forall h_all
    obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := h_exists
    have h_im : (star x ⬝ᵥ (M *ᵥ x)).im = 0 := hM.im_star_dotProduct_mulVec_self x
    have h_re_not_nonneg : ¬ 0 ≤ (star x ⬝ᵥ (M *ᵥ x)).re := by
      intro hle
      have : 0 ≤ star x ⬝ᵥ (M *ᵥ x) := by
        rw [Complex.nonneg_iff]
        exact ⟨hle, h_im.symm⟩
      exact hx this
    have h_re_neg : (star x ⬝ᵥ (M *ᵥ x)).re < 0 :=
      lt_of_not_ge h_re_not_nonneg
    have h_q_neg : star x ⬝ᵥ (M *ᵥ x) < 0 := by
      rw [Complex.neg_iff]
      exact ⟨h_re_neg, h_im⟩
    have hx_ne : x ≠ 0 := by
      intro hx0
      have : star x ⬝ᵥ (M *ᵥ x) = 0 := by simp [hx0]
      rw [this] at h_q_neg
      exact lt_irrefl _ h_q_neg
    have h_exists_coord : ∃ i : n, x i ≠ 0 := by
      by_contra h
      have h_all : ∀ i, x i = 0 := by
        intro i
        by_contra hi
        exact h ⟨i, hi⟩
      have : x = 0 := funext h_all
      exact hx_ne this
    let S : ℝ := ∑ i : n, Complex.normSq (x i)
    have hS_nonneg : 0 ≤ S := Finset.sum_nonneg fun i _ => Complex.normSq_nonneg _
    have hS_pos : 0 < S := by
      have h_nonneg : ∀ i ∈ Finset.univ (α := n), 0 ≤ Complex.normSq (x i) :=
        fun i _ => Complex.normSq_nonneg _
      have h_pos : ∃ i ∈ Finset.univ (α := n), 0 < Complex.normSq (x i) := by
        obtain ⟨i0, hi0⟩ := h_exists_coord
        exact ⟨i0, Finset.mem_univ _, (Complex.normSq_pos).mpr hi0⟩
      exact Finset.sum_pos' h_nonneg h_pos
    let r : ℝ := Real.sqrt S
    have hr_pos : 0 < r := Real.sqrt_pos.mpr hS_pos
    have hr_ne : r ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hr_pos
    have hr_sq : r * r = S := Real.mul_self_sqrt hS_nonneg
    let t : ℝ := r⁻¹
    have ht_pos : 0 < t := inv_pos.mpr hr_pos
    have htr : t * r = 1 := inv_mul_cancel₀ hr_ne
    have ht_sq_mul_S : t * t * S = 1 := by
      calc t * t * S = t * t * (r * r) := by rw [hr_sq]
        _ = (t * r) * (t * r) := by ring
        _ = 1 := by rw [htr, one_mul]
    let c : ℂ := (t : ℂ)
    have hc_star : star c = c := by
      simp [c]
    let y : n → ℂ := fun i => c * x i
    have hy_star : ∀ i, star (y i) = c * star (x i) := by
      intro i
      simp only [y]
      rw [star_mul, hc_star, mul_comm]
    have h_star_y_eq : star y = c • star x := by
      funext i
      simp only [Pi.star_apply, y, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
      rw [star_mul, hc_star, mul_comm]
    have h_mulVec_y : M *ᵥ y = c • (M *ᵥ x) := by
      have : y = c • x := by
        funext i
        simp [y, smul_eq_mul]
      rw [this, Matrix.mulVec_smul]
    have h_eq_star_mul_self : ∀ i, star (x i) * x i = (Complex.normSq (x i) : ℂ) := by
      intro i
      simp only [Complex.star_def]
      rw [← Complex.normSq_eq_conj_mul_self]
    have h_sum_star_x : ∑ i : n, star (x i) * x i = (S : ℂ) := by
      have h1 : ∑ i : n, star (x i) * x i = ∑ i : n, (Complex.normSq (x i) : ℂ) := by
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro i _
        exact h_eq_star_mul_self i
      rw [h1, Complex.ofReal_sum]
    have h_unit_sum : ∑ i : n, star (y i) * y i = 1 := by
      have h1 : ∀ i, star (y i) * y i = (c * c) * (star (x i) * x i) := by
        intro i
        calc star (y i) * y i = (c * star (x i)) * (c * x i) := by rw [hy_star]
          _ = (c * c) * (star (x i) * x i) := by ring
      have h2 : ∑ i : n, star (y i) * y i = (c * c) * ∑ i : n, star (x i) * x i := by
        calc ∑ i : n, star (y i) * y i
            = ∑ i : n, (c * c) * (star (x i) * x i) := Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => h1 i
          _ = (c * c) * ∑ i : n, star (x i) * x i := by rw [Finset.mul_sum]
      rw [h2, h_sum_star_x]
      have hc2 : c * c = ((t * t : ℝ) : ℂ) := by simp [c, Complex.ofReal_mul]
      rw [hc2, ← Complex.ofReal_mul, ht_sq_mul_S]
      simp
    let ψ : Complex.UnitVector n := ⟨y, h_unit_sum⟩
    have h_q_y : star ψ.coord ⬝ᵥ (M *ᵥ ψ.coord) = ((t * t : ℝ) : ℂ) * (star x ⬝ᵥ (M *ᵥ x)) := by
      have h_dot : star y ⬝ᵥ (M *ᵥ y) = (c • star x) ⬝ᵥ (c • (M *ᵥ x)) := by
        rw [h_star_y_eq, h_mulVec_y]
      calc star ψ.coord ⬝ᵥ (M *ᵥ ψ.coord) = star y ⬝ᵥ (M *ᵥ y) := rfl
        _ = (c • star x) ⬝ᵥ (c • (M *ᵥ x)) := h_dot
        _ = c • ((star x) ⬝ᵥ (c • (M *ᵥ x))) := by rw [smul_dotProduct]
        _ = c • (c • (star x ⬝ᵥ (M *ᵥ x))) := by rw [dotProduct_smul]
        _ = (c * c) • (star x ⬝ᵥ (M *ᵥ x)) := by rw [smul_smul]
        _ = ((t * t : ℝ) : ℂ) * (star x ⬝ᵥ (M *ᵥ x)) := by
            have hc2 : c * c = ((t * t : ℝ) : ℂ) := by simp [c, Complex.ofReal_mul]
            rw [hc2, smul_eq_mul]
    have h_q_y_neg : star ψ.coord ⬝ᵥ (M *ᵥ ψ.coord) < 0 := by
      rw [h_q_y]
      have ht2_pos : 0 < t * t := mul_pos ht_pos ht_pos
      let q := star x ⬝ᵥ (M *ᵥ x)
      have h_re : (((t * t : ℝ) : ℂ) * q).re = (t * t) * q.re := by simp [q]
      have h_im_eq : (((t * t : ℝ) : ℂ) * q).im = (t * t) * q.im := by simp [q]
      rw [Complex.neg_iff]
      refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
      · rw [h_re]
        exact mul_neg_of_pos_of_neg ht2_pos h_re_neg
      · rw [h_im_eq, h_im, mul_zero]
    exact ⟨ψ, h_q_y_neg⟩
  · intro hExists hPSD
    obtain ⟨ψ, hψ⟩ := hExists
    have h_nonneg := hPSD.dotProduct_mulVec_nonneg ψ.coord
    have h_not_nonneg : ¬ 0 ≤ star ψ.coord ⬝ᵥ (M *ᵥ ψ.coord) := by
      intro hle
      rw [Complex.nonneg_iff] at hle
      rw [Complex.neg_iff] at hψ
      exact lt_irrefl _ (lt_of_lt_of_le hψ.1 hle.1)
    exact h_not_nonneg h_nonneg

end Matrix

module

public import MathlibExt.Analysis.Matrix.TraceNorm
public import MathlibExt.Analysis.Matrix.TraceNormScalar

/-!
# Trace-norm distance and trace distance for complex matrices

This module defines two distance conventions on square complex matrices
via `Matrix.traceNorm`:

* `Matrix.traceNormDist` – full distance `‖M - N‖₁`.
* `Matrix.traceDist` – standard quantum distance `(1/2)‖M - N‖₁`.

Both are transparent wrappers around `traceNorm`. The proved API comprises
the definitional unfoldings, the half/full inter-convention conversion,
and for each convention nonnegativity, self-distance, symmetry, and
zero-iff-equality.

## Main definitions

* `Matrix.traceNormDist`
* `Matrix.traceDist`

## Main results

* `traceNormDist_def`, `traceDist_def`
* `traceDist_eq_half_traceNormDist`, `traceNormDist_eq_two_mul_traceDist`
* nonnegativity, self, comm, and `= 0 ↔ =` for both conventions.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Matrix

namespace Matrix

variable {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

/-- Full trace-norm distance between square complex matrices: `‖M - N‖₁`. -/
noncomputable def traceNormDist (M N : Matrix n n ℂ) : ℝ :=
  (M - N).traceNorm

@[simp]
theorem traceNormDist_def (M N : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    traceNormDist M N = (M - N).traceNorm := rfl

/-- Standard quantum trace distance `(1/2)‖M - N‖₁`. -/
noncomputable def traceDist (M N : Matrix n n ℂ) : ℝ :=
  (1 / 2 : ℝ) * traceNormDist M N

@[simp]
theorem traceDist_def (M N : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    traceDist M N = (1 / 2 : ℝ) * (M - N).traceNorm := rfl

theorem traceDist_eq_half_traceNormDist (M N : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    traceDist M N = (1 / 2 : ℝ) * traceNormDist M N := rfl

theorem traceNormDist_eq_two_mul_traceDist (M N : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    traceNormDist M N = 2 * traceDist M N := by
  unfold traceDist traceNormDist
  ring

theorem traceNormDist_nonneg (M N : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    0 ≤ traceNormDist M N :=
  traceNorm_nonneg _

theorem traceDist_nonneg (M N : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    0 ≤ traceDist M N := by
  unfold traceDist
  apply mul_nonneg
  · norm_num
  · exact traceNormDist_nonneg _ _

@[simp]
theorem traceNormDist_self (M : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    traceNormDist M M = 0 := by
  simp [traceNormDist]

@[simp]
theorem traceDist_self (M : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    traceDist M M = 0 := by
  simp [traceDist]

theorem traceNormDist_comm (M N : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    traceNormDist M N = traceNormDist N M := by
  unfold traceNormDist
  have h : M - N = -(N - M) := by ext i j; simp
  rw [h, traceNorm_neg]

theorem traceDist_comm (M N : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    traceDist M N = traceDist N M := by
  unfold traceDist
  rw [traceNormDist_comm]

theorem traceNormDist_eq_zero_iff (M N : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    traceNormDist M N = 0 ↔ M = N := by
  rw [traceNormDist_def, traceNorm_eq_zero_iff, sub_eq_zero]

theorem traceDist_eq_zero_iff (M N : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    traceDist M N = 0 ↔ M = N := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    unfold traceDist at h
    have h_half_ne : (1 / 2 : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by norm_num
    have h0 : traceNormDist M N = 0 := by
      have : (1 / 2 : ℝ) * traceNormDist M N = 0 := h
      exact (mul_eq_zero.mp this).resolve_left h_half_ne
    exact (traceNormDist_eq_zero_iff _ _).mp h0
  · rintro rfl
    exact traceDist_self _

end Matrix

/-!
# Finite matrix trace norm

This module defines the trace norm (Schatten-1 norm) for finite square
complex matrices via singular values of the associated linear map.
We choose `Matrix.toEuclideanLin` as the canonical conversion from a
matrix `M : Matrix n n ℂ` to the linear map
`EuclideanSpace ℂ n →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n` given by left multiplication.
This is a linear equivalence, hence injective, and respects the standard
inner product structure on `EuclideanSpace`.

The trace norm is defined as the finite sum of singular values over the
domain dimension. The module establishes nonnegativity, vanishing at zero,
and the characterization of vanishing trace norm as the zero matrix.

## Main definitions

* `Matrix.traceNorm` – trace norm of a square complex matrix.

## Main results

* `Matrix.traceNorm_eq_sum` – unfolding as finite sum.
* `Matrix.traceNorm_nonneg` – nonnegativity.
* `Matrix.traceNorm_zero` – trace norm of zero is zero.
* `Matrix.traceNorm_eq_zero_iff` – trace norm zero iff matrix zero.

## Tags

trace norm, Schatten norm, singular values
-/

@[expose] public section

open Matrix LinearMap Finset Module

namespace Matrix

variable {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

/-- Trace norm of a finite square complex matrix, defined as the sum of
singular values of its associated linear map `Matrix.toEuclideanLin`.
We sum over `Finset.range (Fintype.card n)`, which contains all possibly
nonzero singular values for an `n × n` matrix. -/
noncomputable def traceNorm (M : Matrix n n ℂ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (Fintype.card n),
    (Matrix.toEuclideanLin M).singularValues i

@[simp]
theorem traceNorm_eq_sum (M : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    M.traceNorm = ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (Fintype.card n),
      (Matrix.toEuclideanLin M).singularValues i := rfl

theorem traceNorm_nonneg (M : Matrix n n ℂ) : 0 ≤ M.traceNorm := by
  unfold traceNorm
  apply Finset.sum_nonneg
  intro i _
  exact (Matrix.toEuclideanLin M).singularValues_nonneg i

@[simp]
theorem traceNorm_zero : (0 : Matrix n n ℂ).traceNorm = 0 := by
  unfold traceNorm
  simp

theorem traceNorm_eq_zero_iff (M : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    M.traceNorm = 0 ↔ M = 0 := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    unfold traceNorm at h
    have h_nonneg : ∀ i ∈ Finset.range (Fintype.card n),
        0 ≤ (Matrix.toEuclideanLin M).singularValues i := fun i _ =>
      (Matrix.toEuclideanLin M).singularValues_nonneg i
    have h_sum_zero :=
      (Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg h_nonneg).mp h
    have h_sv_zero : ∀ i, (Matrix.toEuclideanLin M).singularValues i = 0 := by
      intro i
      by_cases hi : i < Fintype.card n
      · have := h_sum_zero i (Finset.mem_range.mpr hi)
        exact this
      · have h_le : Fintype.card n ≤ i := Nat.le_of_not_lt hi
        have h_finrank :
            finrank ℂ (EuclideanSpace ℂ n) = Fintype.card n := by
          simp [finrank_euclideanSpace]
        rw [← h_finrank] at h_le
        exact (Matrix.toEuclideanLin M).singularValues_of_finrank_le h_le
    have h_sv : (Matrix.toEuclideanLin M).singularValues = 0 := by
      ext i
      exact h_sv_zero i
    have h_lin : Matrix.toEuclideanLin M = 0 := by
      rw [LinearMap.singularValues_eq_zero_iff] at h_sv
      exact h_sv
    have h_eq : M = 0 := by
      apply (Matrix.toEuclideanLin : Matrix n n ℂ ≃ₗ[ℂ] _).injective
      simp [h_lin]
    exact h_eq
  · rintro rfl
    exact traceNorm_zero

end Matrix

module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.Matrix.Normed
public import MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.ZeroExtension

/-!
# Top-left zero padding and the supremum-of-row-sums matrix seminorm

The source and target use their existing outer-supremum, inner-L1 matrix
seminorms. Padding retains every row sum and adds only zero rows. Empty
matrices are included; no ring, scalar action or coefficient completeness is
needed. This is not a comparison with a C-star or elementwise matrix norm.
-/

public section

open scoped BigOperators NNReal

namespace Matrix

universe u

/-- Literal top-left zero padding preserves the supremum-of-row-sums
seminorm, with both existing matrix dictionaries specified explicitly. -/
theorem linfty_opNorm_zeroExtend
    {A : Type u} [SeminormedAddCommGroup A]
    {r s : ℕ} (h : r ≤ s) (X : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) A) :
    letI : SeminormedAddCommGroup (Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) A) :=
      Matrix.linftyOpSeminormedAddCommGroup
    letI : SeminormedAddCommGroup (Matrix (Fin s) (Fin s) A) :=
      Matrix.linftyOpSeminormedAddCommGroup
    ‖Matrix.zeroExtend h X‖ = ‖X‖ := by
  classical
  let _ : SeminormedAddCommGroup (Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) A) :=
    Matrix.linftyOpSeminormedAddCommGroup
  let _ : SeminormedAddCommGroup (Matrix (Fin s) (Fin s) A) :=
    Matrix.linftyOpSeminormedAddCommGroup
  obtain ⟨d, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le h
  let Z : Matrix (Fin (r + d)) (Fin (r + d)) A := Matrix.zeroExtend h X
  let a : Fin r → ℝ≥0 := fun i => ∑ j : Fin r, ‖X i j‖₊
  let b : Fin (r + d) → ℝ≥0 := fun i => ∑ j : Fin (r + d), ‖Z i j‖₊
  have hnew (i : Fin (r + d)) (hi : r ≤ i.val) : b i = 0 := by
    change (∑ j : Fin (r + d), ‖Z i j‖₊) = 0
    apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
    intro j _
    rw [show Z i j = 0 from Matrix.zeroExtend_of_row h X i j hi, nnnorm_zero]
  have hrow (i : Fin r) : b (i.castLE h) = a i := by
    change (∑ j : Fin (r + d), ‖Z (i.castLE h) j‖₊) =
      ∑ j : Fin r, ‖X i j‖₊
    calc
      (∑ j : Fin (r + d), ‖Z (i.castLE h) j‖₊) =
          ∑ j : Fin r, ‖Z (i.castLE h) (Fin.castAdd d j)‖₊ := by
        apply Fin.sum_trunc
        intro j
        have hj : r ≤ (Fin.natAdd r j).val := by
          exact Nat.le_add_right r j.val
        rw [show Z (i.castLE h) (Fin.natAdd r j) = 0 from
          Matrix.zeroExtend_of_col h X (i.castLE h) (Fin.natAdd r j) hj,
          nnnorm_zero]
      _ = ∑ j : Fin r, ‖X i j‖₊ := by
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro j _
        have hj : Fin.castAdd d j = j.castLE h := Fin.ext rfl
        rw [hj, show Z (i.castLE h) (j.castLE h) = X i j from
          Matrix.zeroExtend_castLE h X i j]
  have hsup : (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin (r + d))).sup b =
      (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin r)).sup a := by
    apply le_antisymm
    · apply Finset.sup_le
      intro i _
      by_cases hi : i.val < r
      · let i0 : Fin r := ⟨i.val, hi⟩
        have hi0 : i0.castLE h = i := Fin.ext rfl
        rw [← hi0, hrow]
        exact Finset.le_sup (f := a) (Finset.mem_univ i0)
      · rw [hnew i (Nat.le_of_not_gt hi)]
        exact bot_le
    · apply Finset.sup_le
      intro i _
      rw [← hrow i]
      exact Finset.le_sup (f := b) (Finset.mem_univ (i.castLE h))
  change ‖Z‖ = ‖X‖
  calc
    ‖Z‖ = (((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin (r + d))).sup b : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) :=
      Matrix.linfty_opNorm_def Z
    _ = (((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin r)).sup a : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) :=
      congrArg (fun x : ℝ≥0 => (x : ℝ)) hsup
    _ = ‖X‖ := (Matrix.linfty_opNorm_def X).symm

end Matrix

/-

module

public import MathlibExt.Analysis.Normed.Algebra.NonUnitalStarCompletion.Hom

/-!
# Original metric laws for the same completed star hom

An initial norm-preserving hom retains its isometry on the existing completion
extension. The target's original norm and additive metric are kept compatible
by their distance identity; no target associative multiplication or
multiplicative norm estimate is required. Neither a new metric nor a second
extension is constructed, and initial algebraic injectivity is not a premise.
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

namespace NonUnitalStarAlgHom

open UniformSpace.Completion

universe uR uA uB

variable {R : Type uR} {A : Type uA} {B : Type uB}
variable [Monoid R]
variable [NonUnitalSeminormedRing A] [StarRing A] [ContinuousStar A]
variable [DistribMulAction R A] [UniformContinuousConstSMul R A]
variable [NonUnitalNonAssocRing B] [Norm B] [PseudoMetricSpace B]
variable [IsUniformAddGroup B] [CompleteSpace B] [T0Space B]
variable [ContinuousMul B] [Star B] [ContinuousStar B]
variable [DistribMulAction R B] [UniformContinuousConstSMul R B]

/-- The same extension preserves its original norm and metric, and is injective.
The target distance identity concerns its existing additive metric, independently
of the hom; it does not assume a law of the completed extension. -/
theorem fromCompletion_norm_isometry
    (hDistB : ∀ x y : B, dist x y = ‖-x + y‖)
    (φ : A →⋆ₙₐ[R] B) (hφ : Continuous φ)
    (hNorm : ∀ a : A, ‖φ a‖ = ‖a‖) :
    let C := UniformSpace.Completion A;
    let rC : NonUnitalNormedRing C := nonUnitalCompletionNormedRing A;
    letI : NonUnitalNormedRing C := rC;
    let rS : StarRing C := nonUnitalCompletionStarRing A;
    letI : StarRing C := rS;
    let mC : DistribMulAction R C := inferInstance;
    letI : DistribMulAction R C := mC;
    let Γ : C →⋆ₙₐ[R] B := fromCompletion φ hφ;
    (∀ x : C, ‖Γ x‖ = ‖x‖) ∧ Isometry Γ ∧ Function.Injective Γ := by
  let C := UniformSpace.Completion A
  let rC : NonUnitalNormedRing C := nonUnitalCompletionNormedRing A
  let : NonUnitalNormedRing C := rC
  let rS : StarRing C := nonUnitalCompletionStarRing A
  let : StarRing C := rS
  let mC : DistribMulAction R C := inferInstance
  let : DistribMulAction R C := mC
  let Γ : C →⋆ₙₐ[R] B := fromCompletion φ hφ
  change (∀ x : C, ‖Γ x‖ = ‖x‖) ∧ Isometry Γ ∧ Function.Injective Γ
  have hIsoφ : Isometry (φ : A → B) := Isometry.of_dist_eq fun a b => by
    calc
      dist (φ a) (φ b) = ‖-φ a + φ b‖ := hDistB _ _
      _ = ‖φ (-a + b)‖ := by rw [map_add, map_neg]
      _ = ‖-a + b‖ := hNorm _
      _ = dist a b := (NonUnitalSeminormedRing.dist_eq a b).symm
  let φa : A →+ B := AddMonoidHom.ofClass φ
  have hφa : Continuous φa := hφ
  have hFun : (Γ : C → B) = UniformSpace.Completion.extension (φ : A → B) := by
    calc
      (Γ : C → B) = (φa.extension hφa : C → B) := coe_fromCompletion φ hφ
      _ = UniformSpace.Completion.extension (φ : A → B) := rfl
  have hIsoΓ : Isometry Γ := by
    rw [hFun]
    exact hIsoφ.completion_extension
  refine ⟨?_, hIsoΓ, hIsoΓ.injective⟩
  intro x
  have hZero : Γ (0 : C) = (0 : B) := map_zero Γ
  calc
    ‖Γ x‖ = dist (0 : B) (Γ x) := by rw [hDistB, neg_zero, zero_add]
    _ = dist (0 : C) x := by simpa only [hZero] using hIsoΓ.dist_eq (0 : C) x
    _ = ‖x‖ := by rw [NonUnitalNormedRing.dist_eq, neg_zero, zero_add]

end NonUnitalStarAlgHom

end

end

module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Algebra.UnitizationL1
public import Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Algebra.Equiv
public import MathlibExt.Algebra.Algebra.Unitization.Unital

/-!
# The L¹ unitization of an already unital normed algebra

For a unital normed `𝕜`-algebra `A`, its L¹ unitization is continuously
algebra-equivalent to `𝕜 × A`. The equivalence is the shear

`(c, a) ↦ (c, c • 1 + a)`

with inverse `(c, b) ↦ (c, b - c • 1)`. The scalar and algebra coordinates
may live in different universes.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace WithLp

noncomputable section

universe u v

/-- The continuous algebra equivalence from the L¹ unitization of a unital
normed algebra to the product of its scalar field and the algebra. -/
noncomputable def unitalUnitizationProdContinuousAlgEquiv
    (𝕜 : Type u) (A : Type v)
    [NormedField 𝕜] [NormedRing A] [NormedAlgebra 𝕜 A] :
    WithLp 1 (Unitization 𝕜 A) ≃A[𝕜] 𝕜 × A := by
  let eAlg : WithLp 1 (Unitization 𝕜 A) ≃ₐ[𝕜] 𝕜 × A :=
    (WithLp.unitizationAlgEquiv 𝕜).trans
      (Unitization.unitalProdAlgEquiv 𝕜 A)
  refine ContinuousAlgEquiv.mk eAlg ?_ ?_
  · let e : WithLp 1 (Unitization 𝕜 A) ≃ₜ 𝕜 × A :=
      (WithLp.uniformEquiv_unitization_addEquiv_prod 𝕜 A).toHomeomorph.trans
        (WithLp.homeomorphProd 1 𝕜 A)
    have he : Continuous (fun x : WithLp 1 (Unitization 𝕜 A) ↦ e x) :=
      e.continuous
    have hfst : Continuous (fun x : WithLp 1 (Unitization 𝕜 A) ↦ (e x).1) :=
      continuous_fst.comp he
    have hsnd : Continuous (fun x : WithLp 1 (Unitization 𝕜 A) ↦
        (e x).1 • (1 : A) + (e x).2) :=
      (hfst.smul continuous_const).add (continuous_snd.comp he)
    have he_apply (x : WithLp 1 (Unitization 𝕜 A)) :
        e x = ((WithLp.ofLp x).fst, (WithLp.ofLp x).snd) := rfl
    change Continuous (fun x : WithLp 1 (Unitization 𝕜 A) ↦
      Unitization.unitalProdAlgEquiv 𝕜 A (WithLp.unitizationAlgEquiv 𝕜 x))
    simpa only [WithLp.unitizationAlgEquiv_apply,
      Unitization.unitalProdAlgEquiv_apply, he_apply] using hfst.prodMk hsnd
  · let e : WithLp 1 (Unitization 𝕜 A) ≃ₜ 𝕜 × A :=
      (WithLp.uniformEquiv_unitization_addEquiv_prod 𝕜 A).toHomeomorph.trans
        (WithLp.homeomorphProd 1 𝕜 A)
    have hshear : Continuous (fun p : 𝕜 × A ↦
        (p.1, p.2 - p.1 • (1 : A))) :=
      continuous_fst.prodMk
        (continuous_snd.sub (continuous_fst.smul continuous_const))
    have h := e.symm.continuous.comp hshear
    have he_apply (x : WithLp 1 (Unitization 𝕜 A)) :
        e x = ((WithLp.ofLp x).fst, (WithLp.ofLp x).snd) := rfl
    have hpoint (p : 𝕜 × A) :
        e.symm (p.1, p.2 - p.1 • (1 : A)) =
          WithLp.toLp 1
            (Unitization.inl p.1 + Unitization.inr (p.2 - p.1 • (1 : A))) := by
      apply e.injective
      rw [e.apply_symm_apply, he_apply]
      simp [Unitization.inr, Unitization.inl]
    have htarget : Continuous (fun p : 𝕜 × A ↦ WithLp.toLp 1
        (Unitization.inl p.1 + Unitization.inr (p.2 - p.1 • (1 : A)))) := by
      rw [show (fun p : 𝕜 × A ↦ WithLp.toLp 1
        (Unitization.inl p.1 + Unitization.inr (p.2 - p.1 • (1 : A)))) =
        (fun p : 𝕜 × A ↦ e.symm (p.1, p.2 - p.1 • (1 : A))) by
          funext p
          exact (hpoint p).symm]
      exact h
    change Continuous (fun p : 𝕜 × A ↦
      (WithLp.unitizationAlgEquiv 𝕜).symm
        ((Unitization.unitalProdAlgEquiv 𝕜 A).symm p))
    simpa only [Unitization.unitalProdAlgEquiv_symm_apply,
      WithLp.unitizationAlgEquiv_symm_apply] using htarget

@[simp]
theorem unitalUnitizationProdContinuousAlgEquiv_apply_fst
    (𝕜 : Type u) (A : Type v)
    [NormedField 𝕜] [NormedRing A] [NormedAlgebra 𝕜 A]
    (x : WithLp 1 (Unitization 𝕜 A)) :
    (unitalUnitizationProdContinuousAlgEquiv 𝕜 A x).1 =
      (WithLp.ofLp x).fst := by
  change (Unitization.unitalProdAlgEquiv 𝕜 A
    (WithLp.unitizationAlgEquiv 𝕜 x)).1 = _
  rw [Unitization.unitalProdAlgEquiv_apply_fst]
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem unitalUnitizationProdContinuousAlgEquiv_apply_snd
    (𝕜 : Type u) (A : Type v)
    [NormedField 𝕜] [NormedRing A] [NormedAlgebra 𝕜 A]
    (x : WithLp 1 (Unitization 𝕜 A)) :
    (unitalUnitizationProdContinuousAlgEquiv 𝕜 A x).2 =
      (WithLp.ofLp x).fst • (1 : A) + (WithLp.ofLp x).snd := by
  change (Unitization.unitalProdAlgEquiv 𝕜 A
    (WithLp.unitizationAlgEquiv 𝕜 x)).2 = _
  rw [Unitization.unitalProdAlgEquiv_apply_snd]
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem unitalUnitizationProdContinuousAlgEquiv_symm_apply
    (𝕜 : Type u) (A : Type v)
    [NormedField 𝕜] [NormedRing A] [NormedAlgebra 𝕜 A]
    (c : 𝕜) (a : A) :
    (unitalUnitizationProdContinuousAlgEquiv 𝕜 A).symm (c, a) =
      WithLp.toLp 1
        (Unitization.inl c + Unitization.inr (a - c • (1 : A))) := by
  change (WithLp.unitizationAlgEquiv 𝕜).symm
    ((Unitization.unitalProdAlgEquiv 𝕜 A).symm (c, a)) = _
  rw [Unitization.unitalProdAlgEquiv_symm_apply,
    WithLp.unitizationAlgEquiv_symm_apply]

@[simp]
theorem unitalUnitizationProdContinuousAlgEquiv_algebraMap
    (𝕜 : Type u) (A : Type v)
    [NormedField 𝕜] [NormedRing A] [NormedAlgebra 𝕜 A]
    (c : 𝕜) :
    unitalUnitizationProdContinuousAlgEquiv 𝕜 A
        (algebraMap 𝕜 (WithLp 1 (Unitization 𝕜 A)) c) =
      (c, algebraMap 𝕜 A c) := by
  exact (unitalUnitizationProdContinuousAlgEquiv 𝕜 A).commutes c

@[simp]
theorem unitalUnitizationProdContinuousAlgEquiv_inr
    (𝕜 : Type u) (A : Type v)
    [NormedField 𝕜] [NormedRing A] [NormedAlgebra 𝕜 A]
    (a : A) :
    unitalUnitizationProdContinuousAlgEquiv 𝕜 A
        (WithLp.toLp 1 (Unitization.inr a : Unitization 𝕜 A)) =
      (0, a) := by
  change Unitization.unitalProdAlgEquiv 𝕜 A (Unitization.inr a) = (0, a)
  exact Unitization.unitalProdAlgEquiv_inr 𝕜 A a

end

end WithLp

module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Lp.Finsupp
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.Basic
public import Mathlib.Data.Finsupp.SMul

/-!
# The normed structure on the existing finite-support L1 metric

The finite-support carrier and Mathlib's existing L1 metric are retained.
Its norm is the distance from zero, hence the sum of the coordinate norms.
The inherited pointwise scalar operations make it a normed space without
passing to a completion or changing its topology.
-/

public section

noncomputable section

open scoped NNReal

universe u v w

namespace Finsupp

variable {ι : Type u} {E : Type v}

local instance : Fact ((1 : ℝ≥0) ≤ 1) := ⟨le_rfl⟩

private theorem l1DistOnSupport [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    (a b : WithLp (1 : ℝ≥0) (ι →₀ E)) (s : Finset ι)
    (ha : a.ofLp.support ⊆ s) (hb : b.ofLp.support ⊆ s) :
    dist a b = ∑ i ∈ s, dist (a.ofLp i) (b.ofLp i) := by
  classical
  rw [Finsupp.dist_def]
  simp only [NNReal.coe_one, inv_one, Real.rpow_one]
  rw [Finsupp.sum_of_support_subset (s := s) _
    ((Finsupp.support_zipWith).trans (Finset.union_subset ha hb)) _ (by simp)]
  simp only [Finsupp.zipWith_apply]

/-- Translation preserves the existing finite-support L1 distance. -/
theorem l1_dist_add_left [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    (a b c : WithLp (1 : ℝ≥0) (ι →₀ E)) :
    dist (c + a) (c + b) = dist a b := by
  classical
  let s := c.ofLp.support ∪ a.ofLp.support ∪ b.ofLp.support
  have hc : c.ofLp.support ⊆ s :=
    Finset.subset_union_left.trans Finset.subset_union_left
  have ha : a.ofLp.support ⊆ s :=
    Finset.subset_union_right.trans Finset.subset_union_left
  have hb : b.ofLp.support ⊆ s := Finset.subset_union_right
  have hca : (c + a).ofLp.support ⊆ s := by
    simpa only [WithLp.ofLp_add] using
      Finsupp.support_add.trans (Finset.union_subset hc ha)
  have hcb : (c + b).ofLp.support ⊆ s := by
    simpa only [WithLp.ofLp_add] using
      Finsupp.support_add.trans (Finset.union_subset hc hb)
  rw [l1DistOnSupport (c + a) (c + b) s hca hcb,
    l1DistOnSupport a b s ha hb]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro i hi
  simp only [WithLp.ofLp_add, Finsupp.add_apply, dist_add_left]

/-- Mathlib's original finite-support L1 metric, captured before the normed extension. -/
abbrev l1Metric [NormedAddCommGroup E] :
    MetricSpace (WithLp (1 : ℝ≥0) (ι →₀ E)) := inferInstance

/-- The L1 norm uses exactly the existing finite-support distance from zero. -/
instance instL1Norm [NormedAddCommGroup E] : Norm (WithLp (1 : ℝ≥0) (ι →₀ E)) where
  norm x := dist 0 x

/-- The normed additive structure retains Mathlib's original L1 metric. -/
instance instL1NormedAddCommGroup [NormedAddCommGroup E] :
    NormedAddCommGroup (WithLp (1 : ℝ≥0) (ι →₀ E)) :=
  NormedAddCommGroup.ofAddDist (fun _ => rfl)
    (fun x y z => le_of_eq (l1_dist_add_left x y z).symm)

private theorem l1NormedAddCommGroupMetricComputed [NormedAddCommGroup E] :
    (instL1NormedAddCommGroup (ι := ι) (E := E)).toMetricSpace =
      l1Metric (ι := ι) (E := E) := rfl

/-- The normed group has literally the original finite-support L1 metric. -/
theorem l1NormedAddCommGroup_metric_eq [NormedAddCommGroup E] :
    (instL1NormedAddCommGroup (ι := ι) (E := E)).toMetricSpace =
      l1Metric (ι := ι) (E := E) := l1NormedAddCommGroupMetricComputed

private theorem l1NormOnSupport [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    (a : WithLp (1 : ℝ≥0) (ι →₀ E)) (s : Finset ι) (ha : a.ofLp.support ⊆ s) :
    ‖a‖ = ∑ i ∈ s, ‖a.ofLp i‖ := by
  change dist (0 : WithLp (1 : ℝ≥0) (ι →₀ E)) a = _
  rw [l1DistOnSupport 0 a s (by simp) ha]
  simp only [WithLp.ofLp_zero, Finsupp.zero_apply, dist_zero_left]

/-- The norm is the finite sum of the original coordinate norms. -/
theorem l1_norm_eq_sum [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    (a : WithLp (1 : ℝ≥0) (ι →₀ E)) :
    ‖a‖ = a.ofLp.sum (fun _ x => ‖x‖) := by
  classical
  exact l1NormOnSupport a a.ofLp.support (by rfl)

variable {𝕜 : Type w} [NormedField 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]

/-- The existing finite-support L1 norm scales by the original scalar norm. -/
theorem l1_norm_smul (r : 𝕜) (a : WithLp (1 : ℝ≥0) (ι →₀ E)) :
    ‖r • a‖ = ‖r‖ * ‖a‖ := by
  classical
  have hsupport : (r • a).ofLp.support ⊆ a.ofLp.support := by
    simpa only [WithLp.ofLp_smul] using (Finsupp.support_smul (b := r) (g := a.ofLp))
  rw [l1NormOnSupport (r • a) a.ofLp.support hsupport,
    l1NormOnSupport a a.ofLp.support (by rfl), Finset.mul_sum]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro i hi
  simp only [WithLp.ofLp_smul, Finsupp.smul_apply, norm_smul]

/-- The original pointwise scalar action is normed for the same L1 metric. -/
instance instL1NormedSpace : NormedSpace 𝕜 (WithLp (1 : ℝ≥0) (ι →₀ E)) where
  norm_smul_le r a := le_of_eq (l1_norm_smul r a)

end Finsupp

module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Lp.lpHolder

/-!
# Actual unit-coordinate equivalences of square-summable complex families

The actual coordinate map multiplies each coordinate by the given unit
scalar. Its reciprocal family is the inverse, and pointwise norm equality
proves the whole lp-two norm identity. Empty, finite and infinite indices
remain in the same type. No operator/unitary/spectrum output is an input.
-/

@[expose] public section
noncomputable section
namespace MathlibExt.Analysis.Normed.Lp
open scoped ENNReal
universe u

/-- Actual bounded unit-coordinate multiplication on the given lp-two family. -/
def unitCoordinateMap {I : Type u} (beta : I → ℂ) (hunit : ∀ i, ‖beta i‖ = 1) :
    lp (fun _ : I => ℂ) 2 →L[ℂ] lp (fun _ : I => ℂ) 2 :=
  lp.mapCLM 2 (fun i => beta i • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℂ ℂ) (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 1)
    (fun i => by simpa only [norm_smul, ContinuousLinearMap.norm_id, mul_one] using (hunit i).le)

/-- Literal coordinate value of the actual unit map. -/
theorem unitCoordinateMap_apply {I : Type u} (beta : I → ℂ) (hunit : ∀ i, ‖beta i‖ = 1)
    (x : lp (fun _ : I => ℂ) 2) (i : I) : unitCoordinateMap beta hunit x i = beta i * x i := rfl

/-- Given unit scalars are genuinely nonzero. -/
theorem unitCoordinate_ne_zero {I : Type u} (beta : I → ℂ) (hunit : ∀ i, ‖beta i‖ = 1) (i : I) :
    beta i ≠ 0 := by
  intro hz
  have h := hunit i
  rw [hz, norm_zero] at h
  exact zero_ne_one h

/-- The actual reciprocal scalar family is unit valued. -/
theorem inverseUnitCoordinates {I : Type u} (beta : I → ℂ) (hunit : ∀ i, ‖beta i‖ = 1) :
    ∀ i, ‖(beta i)⁻¹‖ = 1 := fun i => by rw [norm_inv, hunit i, inv_one]

/-- The actual reciprocal diagonal is a left inverse. -/
theorem unitCoordinateMap_left_inv {I : Type u} (beta : I → ℂ) (hunit : ∀ i, ‖beta i‖ = 1)
    (x : lp (fun _ : I => ℂ) 2) :
    unitCoordinateMap (fun i => (beta i)⁻¹) (inverseUnitCoordinates beta hunit)
      (unitCoordinateMap beta hunit x) = x := by
  apply lp.ext
  apply funext
  intro i
  rw [unitCoordinateMap_apply, unitCoordinateMap_apply, ← mul_assoc,
    inv_mul_cancel₀ (unitCoordinate_ne_zero beta hunit i), one_mul]

/-- The actual reciprocal diagonal is a right inverse. -/
theorem unitCoordinateMap_right_inv {I : Type u} (beta : I → ℂ) (hunit : ∀ i, ‖beta i‖ = 1)
    (x : lp (fun _ : I => ℂ) 2) :
    unitCoordinateMap beta hunit
      (unitCoordinateMap (fun i => (beta i)⁻¹) (inverseUnitCoordinates beta hunit) x) = x := by
  apply lp.ext
  apply funext
  intro i
  rw [unitCoordinateMap_apply, unitCoordinateMap_apply, ← mul_assoc,
    mul_inv_cancel₀ (unitCoordinate_ne_zero beta hunit i), one_mul]

/-- Actual unit-coordinate map preserves the whole square-summable norm. -/
theorem unitCoordinateMap_norm {I : Type u} (beta : I → ℂ) (hunit : ∀ i, ‖beta i‖ = 1)
    (x : lp (fun _ : I => ℂ) 2) : ‖unitCoordinateMap beta hunit x‖ = ‖x‖ := by
  have he : ∀ i, ‖unitCoordinateMap beta hunit x i‖ = ‖x i‖ := by
    intro i
    rw [unitCoordinateMap_apply, norm_mul, hunit i, one_mul]
  exact le_antisymm
    (lp.norm_mono (by norm_num : (2 : ℝ≥0∞) ≠ 0) (fun i => (he i).le))
    (lp.norm_mono (by norm_num : (2 : ℝ≥0∞) ≠ 0) (fun i => (he i).ge))

/-- Actual unit-coordinate isometric equivalence with its literal reciprocal inverse. -/
def unitCoordinateEquiv {I : Type u} (beta : I → ℂ) (hunit : ∀ i, ‖beta i‖ = 1) :
    lp (fun _ : I => ℂ) 2 ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] lp (fun _ : I => ℂ) 2 where
  toFun := unitCoordinateMap beta hunit
  invFun := unitCoordinateMap (fun i => (beta i)⁻¹) (inverseUnitCoordinates beta hunit)
  left_inv := unitCoordinateMap_left_inv beta hunit
  right_inv := unitCoordinateMap_right_inv beta hunit
  map_add' := (unitCoordinateMap beta hunit).map_add
  map_smul' := (unitCoordinateMap beta hunit).map_smul
  norm_map' := unitCoordinateMap_norm beta hunit

/-- Literal actual forward coordinate of the canonical equivalence. -/
theorem unitCoordinateEquiv_apply {I : Type u} (beta : I → ℂ) (hunit : ∀ i, ‖beta i‖ = 1)
    (x : lp (fun _ : I => ℂ) 2) (i : I) : unitCoordinateEquiv beta hunit x i = beta i * x i := rfl

/-- Literal actual reciprocal coordinate of the canonical inverse. -/
theorem unitCoordinateEquiv_symm_apply {I : Type u} (beta : I → ℂ) (hunit : ∀ i, ‖beta i‖ = 1)
    (x : lp (fun _ : I => ℂ) 2) (i : I) : (unitCoordinateEquiv beta hunit).symm x i = (beta i)⁻¹ * x i := rfl

end MathlibExt.Analysis.Normed.Lp

module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.PiTensorProduct.ProjectiveSeminorm
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorPower.Basic
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Multilinear.Curry

/-!
# Projective seminorm bound for actual tensor-power concatenation

The actual graded product is bounded by the product of the projective
seminorms. The seminormed version is required by the source smooth tensor
seminorm, whose original p need not separate vectors. The two projective
lifts construct the bounded bilinear map from the actual pure-tensor map;
no multiplication bound or norm model is an input.
-/

@[expose] public section
set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
noncomputable section
open scoped TensorProduct BigOperators
namespace TensorPower
universe uK uV
variable {𝕜 : Type uK} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]
variable {V : Type uV} [SeminormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace 𝕜 V]

/-- Actual concatenation of two tensor powers has the projective product bound,
including degenerate seminorms and zero tensor powers. -/
theorem norm_gMul_le {m n : ℕ} (x : TensorPower 𝕜 m V) (y : TensorPower 𝕜 n V) :
    ‖@GradedMonoid.GMul.mul ℕ (fun k => TensorPower 𝕜 k V) _ _ m n x y‖ ≤ ‖x‖ * ‖y‖ := by
  let f : MultilinearMap 𝕜 (fun _ : Fin m => V)
      (MultilinearMap 𝕜 (fun _ : Fin n => V) (TensorPower 𝕜 (m + n) V)) :=
    MultilinearMap.currySum
      ((PiTensorProduct.tprod 𝕜 (s := fun _ : Fin (m + n) => V)).domDomCongr finSumFinEquiv.symm)
  let GM : TensorPower 𝕜 m V →ₗ[𝕜] TensorPower 𝕜 n V →ₗ[𝕜] TensorPower 𝕜 (m + n) V :=
    (TensorProduct.mk 𝕜 _ _).compr₂
      (TensorPower.mulEquiv (R := 𝕜) (M := V) (n := m) (m := n)).toLinearMap
  have hf (a : Fin m → V) (b : Fin n → V) :
      f a b = GM (PiTensorProduct.tprod 𝕜 a) (PiTensorProduct.tprod 𝕜 b) := by
    change f a b = @GradedMonoid.GMul.mul ℕ (fun k => TensorPower 𝕜 k V) _ _ m n
      (PiTensorProduct.tprod 𝕜 a) (PiTensorProduct.tprod 𝕜 b)
    rw [TensorPower.tprod_mul_tprod]
    change PiTensorProduct.tprod 𝕜 (fun i => Sum.elim a b (finSumFinEquiv.symm i)) =
      PiTensorProduct.tprod 𝕜 (Fin.append a b)
    congr 1
    dsimp only [Fin.append, finSumFinEquiv, Equiv.coe_fn_symm_mk]
    apply funext
    apply Fin.addCases <;> simp
  have hfBound (a : Fin m → V) (b : Fin n → V) :
      ‖f a b‖ ≤ (1 * ∏ i, ‖a i‖) * ∏ j, ‖b j‖ := by
    change ‖PiTensorProduct.tprod 𝕜 (fun i => Sum.elim a b (finSumFinEquiv.symm i))‖ ≤ _
    have hprod :
        (∏ i : Fin (m + n), ‖Sum.elim a b (finSumFinEquiv.symm i)‖) =
          (∏ i : Fin m, ‖a i‖) * ∏ j : Fin n, ‖b j‖ := by
      exact ((finSumFinEquiv.symm).prod_comp
        (fun i : Fin m ⊕ Fin n => ‖Sum.elim a b i‖)).trans (by
          simp only [Fintype.prod_sum_type, Sum.elim_inl, Sum.elim_inr])
    simpa only [_root_.one_mul, hprod] using
      PiTensorProduct.projectiveSeminorm_tprod_le (𝕜 := 𝕜)
        (fun i : Fin (m + n) => Sum.elim a b (finSumFinEquiv.symm i))
  let fc := MultilinearMap.mkContinuousMultilinear f 1 hfBound
  let L := (PiTensorProduct.liftIsometry 𝕜 (fun _ : Fin n => V)
    (TensorPower 𝕜 (m + n) V)).toLinearIsometry
  let outer := L.toContinuousLinearMap.compContinuousMultilinearMap fc
  let B := PiTensorProduct.liftIsometry 𝕜 (fun _ : Fin m => V)
    (TensorPower 𝕜 n V →L[𝕜] TensorPower 𝕜 (m + n) V) outer
  have hnorm : ‖B‖ ≤ 1 := by
    have hfc : ‖fc‖ ≤ 1 :=
      MultilinearMap.mkContinuousMultilinear_norm_le f zero_le_one hfBound
    have ho : ‖outer‖ = ‖fc‖ := L.norm_compContinuousMultilinearMap fc
    have hb : ‖B‖ = ‖outer‖ :=
      (PiTensorProduct.liftIsometry 𝕜 (fun _ : Fin m => V)
        (TensorPower 𝕜 n V →L[𝕜] TensorPower 𝕜 (m + n) V)).norm_map outer
    exact hb.trans_le (ho.trans_le hfc)
  have hpure (a : Fin m → V) (b : Fin n → V) :
      B (PiTensorProduct.tprod 𝕜 a) (PiTensorProduct.tprod 𝕜 b) = f a b := by
    dsimp only [B]
    rw [PiTensorProduct.liftIsometry_apply_apply, PiTensorProduct.lift.tprod]
    change outer a (PiTensorProduct.tprod 𝕜 b) = f a b
    have houter : outer a = PiTensorProduct.liftIsometry 𝕜 (fun _ : Fin n => V)
        (TensorPower 𝕜 (m + n) V) (fc a) := by
      simp only [outer, L, ContinuousLinearMap.compContinuousMultilinearMap_coe, Function.comp_apply,
        LinearIsometry.coe_toContinuousLinearMap, LinearIsometryEquiv.coe_toLinearIsometry]
    rw [houter]
    rw [PiTensorProduct.liftIsometry_apply_apply, PiTensorProduct.lift.tprod]
    rfl
  have hvalue : B x y = GM x y := by
    induction x using PiTensorProduct.induction_on with
    | smul_tprod c a =>
      induction y using PiTensorProduct.induction_on with
      | smul_tprod d b =>
        simp only [map_smul, _root_.smul_apply, LinearMap.smul_apply]
        rw [hpure]
        simpa only [_root_.smul_smul, _root_.mul_comm] using
          congrArg (fun z => c • (d • z)) (hf a b)
      | add y₁ y₂ h₁ h₂ =>
        simpa only [map_add] using congrArg₂ (fun a b => a + b) h₁ h₂
    | add x₁ x₂ h₁ h₂ =>
      simpa only [map_add, _root_.add_apply, LinearMap.add_apply] using
        congrArg₂ (fun a b => a + b) h₁ h₂
  change ‖GM x y‖ ≤ ‖x‖ * ‖y‖
  rw [← hvalue]
  calc
    ‖B x y‖ ≤ ‖B x‖ * ‖y‖ := (B x).le_opNorm y
    _ ≤ (‖B‖ * ‖x‖) * ‖y‖ :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (B.le_opNorm x) (norm_nonneg y)
    _ ≤ (1 * ‖x‖) * ‖y‖ := by gcongr
    _ = _ := by rw [_root_.one_mul]

end TensorPower

public import Mathlib.Analysis.LocallyConvex.WithSeminorms
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Group.Quotient

/-!
# Quotient seminorms

This file defines the seminorm induced on a module quotient by a seminorm on
the original module. It proves the infimum formula, identifies quotient balls
with images of balls, and transports a seminorm-generated topology to the
quotient using finite suprema of the original family.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Set Topology
open scoped NNReal Topology

noncomputable section

universe u v

namespace Seminorm

/-- The quotient seminorm induced by `p` on `X ⧸ Y`. -/
noncomputable def quotient
    {𝕜 : Type*} [NormedField 𝕜]
    {X : Type u} [AddCommGroup X] [Module 𝕜 X]
    (p : Seminorm 𝕜 X) (Y : Submodule 𝕜 X) :
    Seminorm 𝕜 (X ⧸ Y) := by
  let _ : SeminormedAddCommGroup X := p.toSeminormedAddCommGroup
  let _ : NormedSpace 𝕜 X :=
    { norm_smul_le := fun a x ↦ le_of_eq (map_smul_eq_mul p a x) }
  exact normSeminorm 𝕜 (X ⧸ Y)

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- The quotient seminorm is the infimum over representatives of the coset. -/
@[simp]
theorem quotient_mkQ
    {𝕜 : Type*} [NormedField 𝕜]
    {X : Type u} [AddCommGroup X] [Module 𝕜 X]
    (p : Seminorm 𝕜 X) (Y : Submodule 𝕜 X) (x : X) :
    p.quotient Y (Y.mkQ x) =
      sInf (Set.range fun y : Y ↦ p (x + (y : X))) := by
  let _ : SeminormedAddCommGroup X := p.toSeminormedAddCommGroup
  let _ : NormedSpace 𝕜 X :=
    { norm_smul_le := fun a z ↦ le_of_eq (map_smul_eq_mul p a z) }
  change ‖(Y.mkQ x : X ⧸ Y)‖ =
    sInf (Set.range fun y : Y ↦ p (x + (y : X)))
  rw [show Y.mkQ x = QuotientAddGroup.mk' Y.toAddSubgroup x from rfl,
    quotient_norm_mk_eq]
  congr 1
  ext r
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨z, hz, hzr⟩
    refine ⟨⟨z, hz⟩, ?_⟩
    change p (x + z) = r at hzr
    exact hzr
  · rintro ⟨z, hzr⟩
    refine ⟨(z : X), z.property, ?_⟩
    change p (x + (z : X)) = r
    exact hzr

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- The quotient image of a seminorm ball is the corresponding quotient
seminorm ball. -/
theorem image_ball_quotient
    {𝕜 : Type*} [NormedField 𝕜]
    {X : Type u} [AddCommGroup X] [Module 𝕜 X]
    (p : Seminorm 𝕜 X) (Y : Submodule 𝕜 X) (ε : ℝ) :
    Y.mkQ '' p.ball 0 ε = (p.quotient Y).ball 0 ε := by
  let _ : SeminormedAddCommGroup X := p.toSeminormedAddCommGroup
  let _ : NormedSpace 𝕜 X :=
    { norm_smul_le := fun a z ↦ le_of_eq (map_smul_eq_mul p a z) }
  ext z
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
    rw [Seminorm.mem_ball, sub_zero]
    change ‖(Y.mkQ x : X ⧸ Y)‖ < ε
    have hx' : ‖x‖ < ε := by
      change p x < ε
      simpa using hx
    exact (Submodule.Quotient.norm_mk_le Y x).trans_lt hx'
  · intro hz
    rw [Seminorm.mem_ball, sub_zero] at hz
    change ‖z‖ < ε at hz
    obtain ⟨x, hx, hxlt⟩ :=
      Submodule.Quotient.norm_mk_lt z (sub_pos.mpr hz)
    refine ⟨x, ?_, hx⟩
    rw [Seminorm.mem_ball, sub_zero]
    change ‖x‖ < ε
    linarith

end Seminorm

namespace WithSeminorms

/-- Finite suprema of a generating seminorm family induce the quotient
topology after passing to their quotient seminorms. -/
theorem quotient
    {𝕜 : Type*} [NormedField 𝕜]
    {X : Type u} [AddCommGroup X] [Module 𝕜 X]
    [TopologicalSpace X]
    {ι : Type v} [Nonempty ι] {p : ι → Seminorm 𝕜 X}
    (hp : WithSeminorms p) (Y : Submodule 𝕜 X) :
    WithSeminorms (fun s : Finset ι ↦ (s.sup p).quotient Y) := by
  let _ : IsTopologicalAddGroup X := hp.isTopologicalAddGroup
  let q : Finset ι → Seminorm 𝕜 (X ⧸ Y) := fun s ↦
    (s.sup p).quotient Y
  have hmap : Filter.map Y.mkQ (𝓝 (0 : X)) = 𝓝 (0 : X ⧸ Y) := by
    rw [← Y.mkQ.map_zero]
    exact Y.isOpenMap_mkQ.map_nhds_eq Y.continuous_mkQ.continuousAt
  have hsource := hp.hasBasis_zero_ball.map Y.mkQ
  rw [hmap] at hsource
  have hsingle : (𝓝 (0 : X ⧸ Y)).HasBasis
      (fun z : Finset ι × ℝ ↦ 0 < z.2)
      (fun z ↦ (q z.1).ball 0 z.2) := by
    refine hsource.congr (fun _ ↦ Iff.rfl) ?_
    intro z _hz
    simpa [q] using (z.1.sup p).image_ball_quotient Y z.2
  apply SeminormFamily.withSeminorms_of_hasBasis q
  refine hsingle.to_hasBasis ?_ ?_
  · rintro ⟨s, ε⟩ hε
    refine ⟨(q s).ball 0 ε, ?_, Subset.rfl⟩
    rw [SeminormFamily.basisSets_iff]
    exact ⟨{s}, ε, hε, by simp⟩
  · intro U hU
    rw [SeminormFamily.basisSets_iff] at hU
    rcases hU with ⟨t, ε, hε, rfl⟩
    apply hsingle.mem_iff.mp
    rw [Seminorm.ball_finset_sup_eq_iInter q t 0 hε]
    change (⋂ i ∈ t, (q i).ball 0 ε) ∈ 𝓝 (0 : X ⧸ Y)
    rw [Filter.biInter_finset_mem]
    intro s _hs
    exact hsingle.mem_iff.mpr ⟨(s, ε), hε, Subset.rfl⟩

end WithSeminorms

end

module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.Basic

/-!
# Continuous radial clipping into the closed unit ball

The radial clipping map rescales a vector only when its norm exceeds one.  It
is continuous, fixes the closed unit ball, and changes approximation to a
unit-ball target by at most a factor of two.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace MathlibExt.Analysis.Normed.Module

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]

/-- Radial clipping into the closed unit ball. -/
noncomputable def radialClip (x : E) : E :=
  (max 1 ‖x‖)⁻¹ • x

/-- Radial clipping is continuous. -/
theorem continuous_radialClip : Continuous (radialClip : E → E) := by
  have hden : Continuous fun x : E ↦ max 1 ‖x‖ :=
    continuous_const.max continuous_norm
  have hne : ∀ x : E, max 1 ‖x‖ ≠ 0 := fun x ↦
    ne_of_gt (zero_lt_one.trans_le (le_max_left 1 ‖x‖))
  exact (hden.inv₀ hne).smul continuous_id

/-- Radial clipping takes values in the closed unit ball. -/
theorem norm_radialClip_le_one (x : E) : ‖radialClip x‖ ≤ 1 := by
  by_cases hx : ‖x‖ ≤ 1
  · simpa [radialClip, max_eq_left hx] using hx
  · have hx' : 1 < ‖x‖ := lt_of_not_ge hx
    have hpos : 0 < ‖x‖⁻¹ := inv_pos.mpr (zero_lt_one.trans hx')
    rw [radialClip, max_eq_right hx'.le, norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs,
      abs_of_pos hpos, inv_mul_cancel₀ (ne_of_gt (zero_lt_one.trans hx'))]

/-- Radial clipping is the identity on the closed unit ball. -/
theorem radialClip_eq_self {x : E} (hx : ‖x‖ ≤ 1) : radialClip x = x := by
  simp [radialClip, max_eq_left hx]

/-- Clipping an approximant increases its distance to a unit-ball target by at
most a factor of two. -/
theorem norm_sub_radialClip_le_two_mul (w z : E) (hw : ‖w‖ ≤ 1) :
    ‖w - radialClip z‖ ≤ 2 * ‖w - z‖ := by
  by_cases hz : ‖z‖ ≤ 1
  · rw [radialClip_eq_self hz]
    nlinarith [norm_nonneg (w - z)]
  · have hz' : 1 < ‖z‖ := lt_of_not_ge hz
    have hznorm : 0 < ‖z‖ := zero_lt_one.trans hz'
    have hinvle : ‖z‖⁻¹ ≤ 1 := (inv_le_one₀ hznorm).2 hz'.le
    have hclip : ‖z - radialClip z‖ = ‖z‖ - 1 := by
      calc
        ‖z - radialClip z‖ = ‖(1 - ‖z‖⁻¹) • z‖ := by
          congr 1
          rw [radialClip, max_eq_right hz'.le]
          symm
          rw [sub_smul, one_smul]
        _ = |1 - ‖z‖⁻¹| * ‖z‖ := norm_smul _ _
        _ = (1 - ‖z‖⁻¹) * ‖z‖ := by
          rw [abs_of_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr hinvle)]
        _ = ‖z‖ - 1 := by
          field_simp
    have hzw : ‖z‖ - 1 ≤ ‖z - w‖ := by
      calc
        ‖z‖ - 1 ≤ ‖z‖ - ‖w‖ := sub_le_sub_left hw ‖z‖
        _ ≤ |‖z‖ - ‖w‖| := le_abs_self _
        _ ≤ ‖z - w‖ := abs_norm_sub_norm_le z w
    calc
      ‖w - radialClip z‖ = ‖(w - z) + (z - radialClip z)‖ := by
        congr 1
        abel
      _ ≤ ‖w - z‖ + ‖z - radialClip z‖ := norm_add_le _ _
      _ ≤ ‖w - z‖ + ‖z - w‖ := add_le_add_right (hclip.trans_le hzw) _
      _ = 2 * ‖w - z‖ := by rw [norm_sub_rev]; ring

end MathlibExt.Analysis.Normed.Module

/-!
# Second countability of the one-point compactification

The actual OnePoint topology is used. Its countable basis combines a
countable basis of the open original space with complements of a compact
exhaustion. Compact and empty original spaces are included.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Set TopologicalSpace Topology

universe uX

namespace OnePoint

/-- A locally compact Hausdorff second-countable space has a second-countable
one-point compactification. This is a plain proof, not a new global instance. -/
theorem secondCountableTopology (X : Type uX) [TopologicalSpace X]
    [T2Space X] [LocallyCompactSpace X] [SecondCountableTopology X] :
    SecondCountableTopology (OnePoint X) := by
  classical
  let K : CompactExhaustion X := CompactExhaustion.choice X
  let tail : ℕ → Set (OnePoint X) := fun n ↦ (some '' K n)ᶜ
  let B : Set (Set (OnePoint X)) :=
    Set.image some '' countableBasis X ∪ range tail
  have hCount : B.Countable :=
    ((countable_countableBasis X).image (Set.image some)).union (countable_range tail)
  have hBasis : IsTopologicalBasis B := by
    apply isTopologicalBasis_of_isOpen_of_nhds
    · intro U hU
      rcases hU with hU | hU
      · obtain ⟨V, hV, rfl⟩ := hU
        exact isOpen_image_coe.2 (isOpen_of_mem_countableBasis hV)
      · obtain ⟨n, rfl⟩ := hU
        exact isOpen_compl_image_coe.2 ⟨(K.isCompact n).isClosed, K.isCompact n⟩
    · intro x U hx hU
      induction x using OnePoint.rec with
      | infty =>
          obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := K.exists_superset_of_isCompact
            ((isOpen_iff_of_mem hx).1 hU).2
          refine ⟨tail n, Or.inr (mem_range_self n), ?_, ?_⟩
          · exact infty_notMem_image_coe
          · intro z hz
            induction z using OnePoint.rec with
            | infty => exact hx
            | coe z =>
                by_contra hzU
                exact hz (mem_image_of_mem some (hn hzU))
      | coe x =>
          obtain ⟨V, hV, hxV, hVU⟩ :=
            (isBasis_countableBasis X).exists_subset_of_mem_open hx
              (hU.preimage continuous_coe)
          refine ⟨some '' V, Or.inl (mem_image_of_mem (Set.image some) hV),
            mem_image_of_mem some hxV, ?_⟩
          rintro z ⟨w, hw, rfl⟩
          exact hVU hw
  exact hBasis.secondCountableTopology hCount

end OnePoint

/-! # Complex continuous maps as a topological ring for the compact-open topology

Joint continuity is tested on every compact subset of the original domain.
No local compactness or separation assumption on that domain is required.
-/

@[expose] public section
noncomputable section
open Filter Set Topology
namespace ContinuousMap
universe u

/-- Compact restrictions give joint ring continuity for complex continuous maps on any topological domain. -/
instance (priority := 100) complexCompactOpenTopologicalRing
    (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] : IsTopologicalRing C(X, ℂ) where
  continuous_add := continuous_add
  continuous_neg := continuous_neg
  continuous_mul := by
    rw [continuous_iff_continuousAt]
    intro p
    change Tendsto (fun q : C(X, ℂ) × C(X, ℂ) => q.1 * q.2)
      (𝓝 p) (𝓝 (p.1 * p.2))
    apply ContinuousMap.tendsto_iff_forall_isCompact_tendstoUniformlyOn.mpr
    intro L hL
    let : CompactSpace L := isCompact_iff_compactSpace.mp hL
    let i : C(L, X) := ⟨Subtype.val, continuous_subtype_val⟩
    have hi : Continuous (fun f : C(X, ℂ) => f.comp i) := i.continuous_precomp
    have ht : Tendsto
        (fun q : C(X, ℂ) × C(X, ℂ) => q.1.comp i * q.2.comp i)
        (𝓝 p) (𝓝 (p.1.comp i * p.2.comp i)) :=
      ((hi.comp continuous_fst).mul (hi.comp continuous_snd)).tendsto p
    apply tendstoUniformlyOn_iff_tendstoUniformly_comp_coe.mpr
    simpa only [← ContinuousMap.mul_comp, ContinuousMap.coe_comp, ContinuousMap.coe_mk,
      Function.comp_apply, i] using
      (ContinuousMap.tendsto_iff_tendstoUniformly.mp ht)

end ContinuousMap

/-!
# Compact-open maps into a discrete space

The compact-open topology on continuous maps from a compact space to a
discrete space is discrete.  The result is exposed as a theorem returning the
typeclass; this file deliberately installs no global instance.

## Main declaration

* `ContinuousMap.discreteTopology_of_compact_domain`
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false

open Set TopologicalSpace

universe u v

namespace ContinuousMap

/-- The compact-open topology on maps from a compact space to a discrete
space is discrete. -/
theorem discreteTopology_of_compact_domain
    {X : Type u} {Y : Type v}
    [TopologicalSpace X] [CompactSpace X]
    [TopologicalSpace Y] [DiscreteTopology Y] :
    DiscreteTopology C(X, Y) := by
  rw [discreteTopology_iff_isOpen_singleton]
  intro f
  let U : Y → Set C(X, Y) := fun y =>
    {g | MapsTo g (f ⁻¹' {y}) {y}}
  have hrange : (range f).Finite :=
    (isCompact_range f.continuous).finite_of_discrete
  have hU : ∀ y ∈ range f, IsOpen (U y) := by
    intro y _
    exact isOpen_setOfPred_mapsTo
      ((isClosed_singleton.preimage f.continuous).isCompact)
      (isOpen_discrete {y})
  have hopen : IsOpen (⋂ y ∈ range f, U y) :=
    hrange.isOpen_biInter hU
  have heq : (⋂ y ∈ range f, U y) = {f} := by
    ext g
    constructor
    · intro hg
      simp only [mem_iInter] at hg
      have hgf : g = f := by
        ext x
        have hm := hg (f x) ⟨x, rfl⟩ rfl
        simpa using hm
      simp [hgf]
    · intro hgf
      have hgf' : g = f := by simpa using hgf
      subst g
      simp only [mem_iInter]
      intro y _ x hx
      exact hx
  rwa [heq] at hopen

end ContinuousMap

/-!
# Endpoint correction on the actual compact-open interval

The curve is corrected at its two endpoints by the literal affine
formula on the existing `TopCat.I`. The whole curve depends jointly
continuously on its original curve and both desired endpoints. If its
original endpoints already match, every original curve value is fixed.
No completeness hypothesis is used.
-/

public section

noncomputable section

universe u

namespace ContinuousMap

variable {E : Type u} [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E] [TopologicalSpace E]
  [IsTopologicalAddGroup E] [ContinuousSMul ℝ E]

/-- The actual endpoint-corrected curve retains the original interval parameter. -/
def endpointCorrection (γ : C(TopCat.I.{u}, E)) (a b : E) : C(TopCat.I.{u}, E) where
  toFun s := γ s +
    (1 - (TopCat.I.homeomorph s : ℝ)) • (a - γ 0) +
    (TopCat.I.homeomorph s : ℝ) • (b - γ 1)
  continuous_toFun := by
    have ht : Continuous (fun s : TopCat.I.{u} => (TopCat.I.homeomorph s : ℝ)) :=
      TopCat.I.homeomorph.continuous.subtype_val
    exact (γ.continuous.add ((continuous_const.sub ht).smul continuous_const)).add
      (ht.smul continuous_const)

private theorem endpointCorrectionApplyComputed (γ : C(TopCat.I.{u}, E)) (a b : E)
    (s : TopCat.I.{u}) :
    endpointCorrection γ a b s = γ s +
      (1 - (TopCat.I.homeomorph s : ℝ)) • (a - γ 0) +
      (TopCat.I.homeomorph s : ℝ) • (b - γ 1) := rfl

/-- Every corrected value is given by the actual original affine endpoint formula. -/
theorem endpointCorrection_apply (γ : C(TopCat.I.{u}, E)) (a b : E)
    (s : TopCat.I.{u}) :
    endpointCorrection γ a b s = γ s +
      (1 - (TopCat.I.homeomorph s : ℝ)) • (a - γ 0) +
      (TopCat.I.homeomorph s : ℝ) • (b - γ 1) :=
  endpointCorrectionApplyComputed γ a b s

private theorem endpointCorrectionZeroComputed (γ : C(TopCat.I.{u}, E)) (a b : E) :
    endpointCorrection γ a b 0 = a := by
  rw [endpointCorrection_apply, TopCat.I.homeomorph_zero]
  change γ 0 + (1 - (0 : ℝ)) • (a - γ 0) + (0 : ℝ) • (b - γ 1) = a
  simp only [sub_zero, one_smul, zero_smul, add_zero]
  abel

/-- The corrected curve starts at the specified actual left endpoint. -/
theorem endpointCorrection_zero (γ : C(TopCat.I.{u}, E)) (a b : E) :
    endpointCorrection γ a b 0 = a := endpointCorrectionZeroComputed γ a b

private theorem endpointCorrectionOneComputed (γ : C(TopCat.I.{u}, E)) (a b : E) :
    endpointCorrection γ a b 1 = b := by
  rw [endpointCorrection_apply, TopCat.I.homeomorph_one]
  change γ 1 + (1 - (1 : ℝ)) • (a - γ 0) + (1 : ℝ) • (b - γ 1) = b
  simp only [sub_self, zero_smul, one_smul, add_zero]
  abel

/-- The corrected curve ends at the specified actual right endpoint. -/
theorem endpointCorrection_one (γ : C(TopCat.I.{u}, E)) (a b : E) :
    endpointCorrection γ a b 1 = b := endpointCorrectionOneComputed γ a b

private theorem endpointCorrectionSelfComputed (γ : C(TopCat.I.{u}, E)) :
    endpointCorrection γ (γ 0) (γ 1) = γ := by
  apply ContinuousMap.ext
  intro s
  rw [endpointCorrection_apply]
  simp only [sub_self, smul_zero, add_zero]

/-- Correction fixes the entire original curve when given its original endpoints. -/
theorem endpointCorrection_self (γ : C(TopCat.I.{u}, E)) :
    endpointCorrection γ (γ 0) (γ 1) = γ := endpointCorrectionSelfComputed γ

/-- Matching endpoint equations leave every value of the original curve unchanged. -/
theorem endpointCorrection_eq_self (γ : C(TopCat.I.{u}, E)) (a b : E)
    (h₀ : γ 0 = a) (h₁ : γ 1 = b) : endpointCorrection γ a b = γ := by
  rw [← h₀, ← h₁]
  exact endpointCorrection_self γ

private theorem endpointCorrectionContinuous :
    Continuous (fun p : C(TopCat.I.{u}, E) × E × E =>
      endpointCorrection p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2) := by
  apply ContinuousMap.continuous_of_continuous_uncurry
  change Continuous (fun z : (C(TopCat.I.{u}, E) × E × E) × TopCat.I.{u} =>
    z.1.1 z.2 +
      (1 - (TopCat.I.homeomorph z.2 : ℝ)) • (z.1.2.1 - z.1.1 0) +
      (TopCat.I.homeomorph z.2 : ℝ) • (z.1.2.2 - z.1.1 1))
  have ht : Continuous (fun z : (C(TopCat.I.{u}, E) × E × E) × TopCat.I.{u} =>
      (TopCat.I.homeomorph z.2 : ℝ)) :=
    (TopCat.I.homeomorph.continuous.comp continuous_snd).subtype_val
  have hγ : Continuous (fun z : (C(TopCat.I.{u}, E) × E × E) × TopCat.I.{u} =>
      z.1.1 z.2) := continuous_fst.fst.eval continuous_snd
  have h₀ : Continuous (fun z : (C(TopCat.I.{u}, E) × E × E) × TopCat.I.{u} =>
      z.1.1 (0 : TopCat.I.{u})) := (continuous_eval_const _).comp continuous_fst.fst
  have h₁ : Continuous (fun z : (C(TopCat.I.{u}, E) × E × E) × TopCat.I.{u} =>
      z.1.1 (1 : TopCat.I.{u})) := (continuous_eval_const _).comp continuous_fst.fst
  have ha : Continuous (fun z : (C(TopCat.I.{u}, E) × E × E) × TopCat.I.{u} =>
      z.1.2.1) := continuous_fst.snd.fst
  have hb : Continuous (fun z : (C(TopCat.I.{u}, E) × E × E) × TopCat.I.{u} =>
      z.1.2.2) := continuous_fst.snd.snd
  exact (hγ.add ((continuous_const.sub ht).smul (ha.sub h₀))).add (ht.smul (hb.sub h₁))

/-- The whole corrected curve depends jointly continuously on its curve and both endpoints. -/
theorem continuous_endpointCorrection :
    Continuous (fun p : C(TopCat.I.{u}, E) × E × E =>
      endpointCorrection p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2) := endpointCorrectionContinuous

end ContinuousMap
